name: Yartar
summary: Walled trading city and baronry on the east bank of the River Surbrin near its meeting with the Dessarin, where the Evermoor Way crosses by a fortified bridge to the Shield Tower citadel on the west bank; caravans, river barges, fishing and barge-building, ruled by an elected Waterbaron.

identity.subregion: Savage Frontier; east bank of the River Surbrin, overlooking the nearby River Dessarin
identity.ruler_office: Waterbaron, elected for life (Nestra Ruthiol, circa 1491 DR)

periods.lore_2e: 1361 to 1372 DR (Volo's Guide to the North, 1993; The North, 1996)
periods.snapshot_5e: circa 1491 DR (Princes of the Apocalypse, Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide, Storm King's Thunder)
periods.video_game: 1492 DR (Baldur's Gate III, video game only)
periods.note: Nothing is verified for 1492 DR itself.

position.note: Taken from maps/locations.json; not a canonical georeference.

engine_record.population_note: Gazetteer estimate with no reference year. The only sourced figure is 6,000 in 1366 DR (Y4).
engine_record.business_note: Lionshield Coster (HQ) is the only market business headquartered here. Its Phandalin and Triboar branches are separate records (Y14).

area_geography.summary: East-bank city; fortified two-wagon bridge to the Shield Tower citadel on the west bank, where the Evermoor Way crosses the Surbrin; the Dessarin joins from the east; the Surbrin Trail runs north along the east bank toward the ruins of Nesme; the Hiring Fair field lies north of the city.
area_geography.road_distance_note: Everlund and Silverymoon distances are Evermoor Way figures from the wiki (Silver Marches, 2002, p. 85); Triboar and the junction are engine figures.
area_geography.orientation: North is unconfirmed on the area sketch; the 15th-century area map has Triboar to the west and Flint Rock to the north-east.
sources: Volo's Guide to the North, p. 93

labels: The Happy Hall of Fortuitous Happenstance

positions.coordinates: Approximate centres and footprints read by eye from the stored image, in its own pixels, origin top left, x east and y south (640 by 510 for the plan area); not exact

buildings.name: The Happy Hall of Fortuitous Happenstance

layout: The Waterbaron's Hall (1) is the large building at the top centre, with the market stalls (2) in front of it at the centre
The Market is a maze of small stalls between the Hall and the shops to the south

Inns and shops ring the stalls: the Pearl-Handled Pipe (14) to the west, the Wink and the Kiss (7) and the Cointoss (12) to the east, One Foot in the Boat (5), Halassa's (3), Winter Winds (4) and Hasklar's (6) to the south
Beldabar's Rest (11) is a building on the south-east of the square; the sources also place it under the central market
uncertain_readings: Positions and sizes are estimates from a 640 px image
The legend names are circa 1370 DR; not verified for 1492 DR

sketch.method: Three panels. A: crossing, read from the c.1372 and 15th-century area maps and the text, drawn by eye. B: whole city; sourced features only (east-bank walled city, fortified bridge, Shield Tower with covered docks, Fishyard in front of the Waterbaron's Hall, Hiring Fair field north, Surbrin Trail on the east bank); wall circuit, gate positions and quay and barge-yard positions are assumed and labelled so; no scale. C: the 15 plan buildings at the approximate positions in town_plan, scaled by 1.15, stall maze unplotted.
sketch.status: Working reconstruction, not a copy of a published map
